sen_slope.name: Sen slope
sen_slope.definition: The median of the slopes between every pair of years, so a few unusual years barely move it.
sen_slope.meaning: The typical change per year, shown here per decade.

mann_kendall.name: Mann–Kendall test
mann_kendall.definition: A test that counts how often later years sit above or below earlier years, corrected for one year carrying over into the next (Hamed–Rao, lag 1).
mann_kendall.meaning: It decides whether a rise or fall is clear enough to call significant.

p_value.name: p-value
p_value.definition: How likely a trend at least this strong would be by chance if nothing were changing; not the chance that the trend is real.
p_value.meaning: Below 0.05, and with a confidence interval that leaves out zero, the app calls the trend significant.

confidence_interval.name: Confidence interval
confidence_interval.definition: The range of rates the data support; across repeated studies, 95% of such ranges would hold the true rate.
confidence_interval.meaning: When the range includes zero, the data cannot rule out no change.

ols_cross_check.name: OLS cross-check
ols_cross_check.definition: A straight line fitted by least squares, with its interval widened for autocorrelation.
ols_cross_check.meaning: A second method. When it disagrees with the Mann–Kendall test, the card says so.

autocorrelation.name: Autocorrelation
autocorrelation.definition: One year's value carrying over into the next, which makes chance trends look stronger.
autocorrelation.meaning: The tests correct for it, so a run of similar years alone does not make a trend.

anomaly.name: Anomaly
anomaly.definition: The difference between a month's value and the usual value of that month over the record.
anomaly.meaning: It takes out the seasonal cycle, so the chart shows the change and not summer and winter.

scatter.name: Scatter
scatter.definition: How far the yearly values spread around the trend line, as a standard deviation.
scatter.meaning: A large scatter needs a longer record before a trend shows, and a small change can matter little against it.

years_needed.name: Years needed
years_needed.definition: An estimate of how many years of data a test would need to detect a trend of this size, given the scatter and the autocorrelation.
years_needed.meaning: A detection estimate, not a forecast: it says nothing about what will happen.

found_by_scan.name: Found by a scan
found_by_scan.definition: A result that came up when the app tested many variables at once, corrected for multiple testing (Benjamini–Hochberg).
found_by_scan.meaning: Treat it as a lead to check, not as a finding on its own.

record_too_short.name: Record too short
record_too_short.definition: The series holds fewer years than the minimum record of the variable, 20 years by default.
record_too_short.meaning: The app shows the statistics and gives no verdict.

model_data.name: Model data
model_data.definition: Values computed by a weather model that blends in observations, not readings from instruments at this place.
model_data.meaning: Read them as estimates. Cards label them “model”, not “observation”.

power_merra2.name: NASA POWER and MERRA-2
power_merra2.definition: NASA POWER serves analysis-ready meteorology and solar data for any place on Earth, mostly derived from MERRA-2, from 1981. MERRA-2 is NASA's reanalysis, which blends satellite and ground observations with a weather model to rebuild past weather, from 1980.
power_merra2.meaning: Every number in this app comes from these data.

area_mean.name: Area mean and cells
area_mean.definition: POWER divides the Earth into grid cells of ½° latitude by ⅝° longitude. The value of an area is the mean of the cells whose centers fall inside it, weighted by the cosine of latitude.
area_mean.meaning: When no cell center falls inside a small area, the app uses the one cell that contains it.

data_moved.name: Data moved
data_moved.definition: How much stored data the analysis read, and whether the answer came from the cache of stored results.
data_moved.meaning: The analysis runs next to the data in the cloud, and your browser receives only the result.

not_independent.name: Yearly values are not independent
not_independent.definition: The climate of one year often carries over into the next, so the yearly values are not separate draws.
not_independent.meaning: Treating them as independent would call chance trends significant too often, so the tests correct for it.
